newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea says it won't be shaken by defector.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says it won't be shaken by defector.

text.p: North Korea, in its first reaction to Hwang Jang-yop's arrival in Seoul, on Tuesday branded the high-level defector a "cowardly traitor" whose actions will not shake the Stalinist state.
"No matter how much the faithless and cowardly traitor runs frantically about, we will never be shaken," said state-run Radio Pyongyang in report monitored by Tokyo-based Radiopress news agency.
The statement, carried in what was purportedly a letter addressed to North leader Kim Jong-il from a student at Kim Il-sung University, did not mention Hwang by name.
The term "cowardly traitor" was also used when Hwang defected more than two months ago by the media in Pyongyang, which are believed not to have broadcast the defection news domestically.
"It does not matter even if we cannot eat enough nor wear good clothing, so long as General Kim Jong-Il is with us, we can take heart and find strength," the student wrote in a letter dated April 1.
Hwang, who once headed Kim Il-sung University, sought asylum at the South Korean embassy in Beijing on February 12, arriving in Seoul last Sunday after a one-month stay in the Philippines.

Hwang, the highest-ranking North Korean official ever to defect to the South, has in essays written since his defection and carried in the South Korean press described Pyongyang as a feudalistic and militaristic state bent on invading the South.
The North Korean student quoted by Radio Pyongyang wrote that in the event of war, "I shall change my pen for a gun and defend Gen. Kim Jong-il at the front line."
